gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the US Dometic CFX5 45 (R1234yf, SKU 97000050755) is rated at 1.05 Ah/h (about 302 Wh/day at 90°F ambient, 39°F inside), 38% more than the 0.76 Ah/h Dometic gives for the AU/NZ R600a version. They also don't say that the other makers state power on bases you can't compare: Anker gives runtime at 77°F with an empty cooler in Eco mode, and ICECO gives kWh per 24 h with no ambient temperature.
standout_why: I opened the cited OutdoorGearLab page (2025-07-28). It measured DC draw in a 75°F lab (CFX5 45 steady 6.8 W, Anker EverFrost 40 5.8 W, BougeRV 23 qt 8.3 W). It puts the maker 'wattage' row next to those measurements without converting it. It doesn't name the refrigerant variant it tested, and it never mentions that Dometic's US rating differs from the AU/EU rating. I couldn't open gearandhome.com (cited; SSL error) or caranddriver.com (fetch blocked), so I'm judging against OGL only. The point stands out, but it doesn't flip a pick.
decides: This keeps Dometic as the premium pick but changes the power-station sizing. Converted to Wh/day, the US CFX5 45's own rating is about 302 Wh/day at 90°F, so a 500 Wh station covers about 1.7 days before DC-conversion losses. Anker's claim works out to about 134 Wh/day, but that is at 77°F, so it doesn't mean the Anker is more than twice as efficient. On the one common basis we have (OGL's 75°F lab), the measured gap is small: 5.8 W vs 6.8 W. In the table, the footnote is the finding: makers quote power at 77°F, at 90°F and at no stated temperature, and the US and AU versions of the same Dometic carry different ratings.

findings.label: Rated energy consumption, 12 V DC
findings.source_title: Dometic CFX5 45 Electric Cooler (Published Markets: CA, US; 'CFX545, UL plug, USA, AC/DC')
findings.note: Spec line: 'Energy Consumption 12VDC (Ambient@32C, Internal@4C), [Ah/h] 1.05'. Refrigerant R1234yf, GWP 0.5, rated AC input 49 W. My arithmetic: 1.05 × 12 V = 12.6 W; × 24 h = 302 Wh.

findings.label: Rated energy consumption, same test conditions
findings.note: Same basis (32°C ambient, 4°C internal). Refrigerant R600a, rated AC input 43 W. 1.05 / 0.76 = 1.38, so the US unit is rated 38% higher. Any efficiency figure quoted from non-US Dometic literature understates the US model.

findings.label: Stated volume vs measured
findings.value: 46 L stated (IEC 62552-3 total volume) vs 39.6 L (40 qt) measured by OutdoorGearLab
findings.note: The 39.6 L figure comes from OutdoorGearLab's spec table (https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-powered-cooler, read 2026-11-08), which says it used 12-oz cans to measure volume. The IEC 'total volume' is the gross cavity figure, so the gap is about 14%.

findings.label: Runtime claim, converted to average draw
findings.value: 4.3 days on 2 × 288 Wh ≈ 5.6 W average (≈134 Wh/24 h); 52 h on 1 battery ≈ 5.5 W
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX EverFrost 2 40L Electric Cooler (42 qt) – Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Footnote conditions: 39°F inside, empty cooler, Eco mode, 77°F ambient, which is 13°F cooler than Dometic's test. The page gives no conditions for the 52 h figure. My arithmetic: 576 Wh / 103.2 h = 5.6 W. The page states no power consumption figure.

findings.label: Rated energy consumption
findings.note: The manual gives no ambient temperature and calls the figure 'only suitable for laboratory testing'. Its accessories table also lists 0.4348/0.416 kWh/24 h, which contradicts the 0.348. Capacity is 47.0 qt / 45.0 L, range 0°F to 50°F. Don't compare this to Dometic's 90°F figure.

findings.label: Measured steady-state DC draw
findings.value: Dometic CFX5 45 6.8 W; Anker EverFrost 40 (gen 1) 5.8 W; BougeRV 23 qt 8.3 W; 6-hour energy 41 / 35 / 50 Wh
findings.source_title: The Best Electric Coolers | Lab Tested & Ranked (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.note: This is the only common basis across brands. OGL doesn't say which CFX5 45 refrigerant variant it tested, and it tested the first-gen EverFrost, not the EverFrost 2.
